Name: Establishing a universal application system for the senior citizen rent increase exemption program and disability rent increase exemption program.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing a universal application system for the senior citizen rent increase exemption program and disability rent increase exemption program

Summary: This bill would require the creation of an electronic universal application system for the Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE) program and Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE) program, to be administered jointly by the Department of Finance (DOF) and the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD), by July 1, 2028. Additionally, the bill would require participating agencies promote public awareness of the application system on any website related to public assistance or a rent increase exemption program.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subdivision m of section 26-405 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new paragraph (10) to read as follows:
(10) Universal application system. (a) In accordance with subdivision e of section 26-509 and section 26-606.2, the department of finance shall collaborate with the department of housing preservation and development and any other agency designated by the mayor to establish and maintain an electronic common system for applications for a rent increase exemption order pursuant to this subdivision, subdivision e of section 26-509 and section 26-606.2. Such application system shall: 
(i) Accept an application including any relevant documentation submitted electronically; 
(ii) Route an accepted application to the agency responsible for processing such application; and
(iii) Include a publicly accessible web portal with a single user interface through which an applicant may:
(a) Determine the status of an existing or prior rent increase exemption order related to such applicant;
(b) Submit and track the status of an application; 
(c) Send and receive correspondence with the department of finance in relation to such existing or prior rent increase exemption order or an application; and
(d) Ascertain the status and renewal deadline for an existing rent increase exemption order.
(b) An application shall be deemed to have been received on the date upon which it is submitted to such application system.
(c) An applicant may submit a paper application for a rent increase exemption order directly to the department of finance.
§ 2. Section 26-509 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new subdivision e to read as follows:
e. Universal application system. (1) In accordance with paragraph (10) of subdivision m of section 26-405 and section 26-606.2, the department of finance shall collaborate with the department of housing preservation and development and any other agency designated by the mayor to establish and maintain an electronic common system for applications for a rent increase exemption order pursuant to this section, paragraph (10) of subdivision m of section 26-405 and section 26-606.2. Such application system shall:  
(i) Accept an application including any relevant documentation submitted electronically; 
(ii) Route an accepted application to the agency responsible for processing such application; and
(iii) Include a publicly accessible web portal with a single user interface through which an applicant may:
(a) Determine the status of an existing or prior rent increase exemption order related to such applicant;
(b) Submit and track the status of an application; 
(c) Send and receive correspondence with the department of finance in relation to such existing or prior rent increase exemption order or an application; and
(d) Ascertain the status and renewal deadline for an existing rent increase exemption order.
(2) An application shall be deemed to have been received on the date upon which it is submitted to such application system.
(3) An applicant may submit a paper application for a rent increase exemption order directly to the department of finance.
§ 3. Chapter 7 of title 26 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 26-606.2 to read as follows:
§ 26-606.2 Universal application system. a. In accordance with paragraph (10) of subdivision m of section 26-405 and subdivision e of section 26-509, the supervising agency shall collaborate with the department of finance and any other agency designated by the mayor to establish and maintain an electronic common system for applications for a rent increase exemption order pursuant to this chapter, paragraph (10) of subdivision m of section 26-405, and subdivision e of section 26-509. Such application system shall: 
1. Accept an application and any other relevant documentation submitted electronically; 
2. Route an accepted application to the supervising agency or another agency responsible for processing such application; and
3. Include a publicly accessible web portal with a single user interface through which an applicant may:
(a) Determine the status of an existing or prior rent increase exemption order related to such applicant;
(b) Submit and track the status of an application; 
(c) Send and receive correspondence with the supervising agency in relation to such existing or prior rent increase exemption order or an application; and
(d) Ascertain the status and renewal deadline for an existing rent increase exemption order.
b. An application shall be deemed to have been received on the date upon which it is submitted to such application system.
c. An applicant may submit a paper application for a rent increase exemption order directly to the supervising agency or another agency if such agency is responsible for processing such application.
§ 4.  Public awareness. The commissioner of finance and the commissioner of housing preservation and development, in collaboration with any other agency designated by the mayor, shall promote public awareness of the universal application system required by paragraph (10) of subdivision m of section 26-405, subdivision e of section 26-509, and section 26-606.2 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by sections one, two, and three of this local law, respectively, including, but not necessarily limited to, including a link to the web portal required by such paragraph (10), subdivision e, and section 26-606.2 on any city website relating to a public assistance program or a rent increase exemption program authorized by chapter 3, 4, or 7 of title 26 of the administrative code of the city of New York.
§ 5. This local law takes effect July 1, 2028, except that the commissioner of finance and the commissioner of housing preservation and development may take any steps necessary to effectuate the provisions of section four of this local law before such date.
